liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Let It Grow** (3 reviews): Let It Grow with the horns is a standout of the show; Let It Grow is the highlight of the show, which has sharp horn playing [9][11][20]
- **Here Comes Sunshine** (2 reviews): Here Comes Sunshine is called a rare version; Here Comes Sunshine includes a cool exploratory jam [10][18]
- **He's Gone** (2 reviews): He's Gone is described as especially slinky and sweet; He's Gone seems average until the band lifts it in the second half, leading into Truckin' [9][11]
- **Big Railroad Blues** (1 review): Big Railroad Blues is called a rare version [10]
- **Brown Eyed Women** (1 review): Brown Eyed Women is played in a mellow early style [18]
- **Loose Lucy** (1 review): Loose Lucy is praised as a strong performance [18]
- **Playing In The//Band** (1 review): Playin' in the Band is singled out as a killer version [10]

## Setlist highlights

- **tech problem**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 3 archived performances [21]
- **Let Me Sing Your Blues Away**: rare: 8 archived performances [21]
- **Part 1**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 10 archived performances [21]
- **Part II (Let It Grow)**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]

## The recordings

- **gd1973-09-21.145131.sbd.boswell.smith.sirmick.flac1644** (recommended): soundboard; 24 songs; 182 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1973-09-21.143101.sbd.boswell.sirmick.smith.flac2496**: soundboard; 24 songs; 182 min [2]
- **gd73-09-21.sbd.miller.17410.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 21 songs; 166 min; rated 4.62/5 by 21 [5]. Said about its sound: The soundboard is somewhat hissier than some others but still good; Kreutzman's drums are clear in the mix, with clean snare and kick interaction; Vocals are slightly off in places [9][13][14]
- **gd1973-09-21.d3t6.unknown.33567.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 1 songs; 5 min; rated 4/5 by 4 [8]. Said about its sound: This copy cuts out halfway through a song's second chorus and resumes near the end [15]

## Around the show

- Joe Ellis on trumpet and Martin Fierro on saxophone played from Let Me Sing through Let It Grow [14]
- Joe Ellis and Martin Fierro play horns at this show [15]
- Joe Ellis on trumpet and Martin Fierro on saxophone joined for Let Me Sing Your Blues Away [1]
- Doug Sahm opened the show [2]
- Martin Fierro and Joe Ellis played horns on Let Me Sing, Weather Report Suite, Let It Grow and Casey Jones [2]
- Joe Ellis played trumpet and Martin Fierro saxophone [3]
- Horns appear on Let Me Sing, the Weather Report Suite, Let It Grow, and Casey Jones [5]
- The Spectrum had a low-key, peaceable vibe, and its parking lot stayed calm until the 1990s [24]
- The Wharf Rat is said to rival the one from 3/26/73 [11]
- With no second drummer overshadowing him, Bill stands out more than in other shows of the period [13]
- The horn section appeared at only a couple of shows [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1973-09-21.145131.sbd.boswell.smith.sirmick.flac1644**: taped by Will Boswell; transferred by Matt Smith & Sirmick; source: Most likely MR > R @3 & 3/4 ips - dub of Jerry's reel left at a girlfriend's house done by Will Boswell back in the Spring of '79 [1]. Also: Reels came from Will Boswell, transferred by Matt Smith, with pitch correction help from Joe B. Jones; 16 bit, 44.1; Gaps in One More Saturday Night (likely reel flip) and Let Me Sing were closed, and some distortion removed [1]
- **gd1973-09-21.143101.sbd.boswell.sirmick.smith.flac2496**: taped by Will Boswell; transferred by Matt Smith and Sirmick; source: Most likely MR > R @3 & 3/4 ips - dub of Jerry's reel left at a girlfriend's house done by Will Boswell back in the Spring of '79 [2]. Also: A probable reel-flip gap in the encore was closed, with unknown material missing [2]
- **gd73-09-21.sbd.miller.17410.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [5]. Also: Chain: soundboard to reel to PCM to DAT, then Sony R500, Samplitude, Cool Edit, CD, EAC, SHN by Charlie Miller [5]
- **gd1973-09-21.d3t6.unknown.33567.sbeok.flac16**: source: Unknown [8]
